newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK VSZ STEEL HOPES TO LURE TOYOTA DEAL.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK VSZ STEEL HOPES TO LURE TOYOTA DEAL.

text.p: VSZ a.s., Slovakia's largest steel maker, is preparing extensive restructuring measures, partly in the hope of forging new ties with Japan's Toyota Motor Corp.
In an interview with the independent daily Pravda, VSZ Supervisory Board Chairman Alexander Rezes said the changes would benefit Slovakia as a whole.

Asked whether this meant participation in rumoured plans Toyota has to build a car production plant in Slovakia, or a joint venture with the car maker, Rezes replied: "I see that you are well informed".
He did not elaborate on the changes, nor on the possibility of cooperating with Toyota.
After a trip to Japan at the beginning of April, Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said Toyota was considering locating a car plant in eastern Slovakia.
Toyota has not commented on the plant.
VSZ is Slovakia's largest industrial complex with some 100 subsidiaries and daughter companies in various industrial sectors.

The company has been carrying out an expansive investment programme over the past two years, investing heavily not only into its main steel production, but also making purchases ranging from soccer clubs to banks and insurers in Slovakia.
Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar visited Japan earlier this year where he held talks with major Japanese industrial firms on investment prospects in Slovakia.
